text: Odd smell distracts you. You can try to attack next round.
Try to look like you meant to do that. You make no attack this round.
You slip, but keep your feet. Suffer a -3 initiative penalty next round.
Somehow, you manage to strike yourself for 1d10 hits.
Suddenly, the world just seems too confusing. Spend the next round Stunned.
Instinct is not always as reliable as it is made out to be. Your attacks are at -30 for the next three rounds.
Execute the declared attack on the nearest ally, whoops! If no ally is in reach, an innocent bystander will do. Failing that, attack an imaginary friend.
Such an itch! Spend the next two rounds Concentrating on scratching. Hope that it is not fleas.
Survival of the fittest, right? That might not be you. The fight is going out of you as you take a -15 Fatigue penalty.

Bite the inside of your own mouth for 1d10 hits and a round of Stunned unable to parry followed by a round of Stun. The good news is that foes within 10' of you must save versus a level 1 Fear effect.
You take a tumble, traveling 2d10 feet in a random direction. You are also Stunned for the rest of this round and the whole of the next. Hope that your foe is just as surprised.
You got your target's tail! Wait, no, that was your own tail. Take 2d10 hits and a round of Stunned followed by a round of Dazed.
You look in one direction, move in another, and therefore fail to spot the obstacle in your path. You not only lose your attack, but take an 'A' Unbalancing critical.
Where did he go? You managed to get turned around. Your foe is now behind you and gets a free attack on your back.
